utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is Case Number IT-03-72-A, The Prosecutor versus Milan Babic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: May I please have appearances, Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCKEON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Senior trial attorney Mark McKeon for the Prosecution, and I am at counsel table with legal officer, Xavier Tracol, and our case manager, Susan Grogan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUELLER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Peter Michael Mueller from Munich, lead counsel for Mr. Babic, and Mr. Robert Fogelnest from New York as co-counsel. May I ask you a favour, Madam, please. Would you permit me to wear my sunglasses. I underwent a laser operation on my left eye. It would feel much more comfortable if I could wear it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, please. We need counsel's eyes sharp. You may go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUELLER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: May I ask Mr. Milan Babic whether he can understand the proceedings. THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you, please sit down. These proceedings are convened according to Rule 65 bis, subparagraph (b). It is the first Status Conference since the notice of appeal was filed by the appellant. And the purpose of the Status Conference is to find out any matters concerning the health of the appellant and the matters of detention pertaining to the appellant and any other matters that the parties may raise. I note that the filings are going on on time so far. We've had the notice of appeal and the brief, and the other pleadings will follow according to the Rules as the parties are aware. And as far as motions are concerned, we have none which are pending. I would like to ask Mr. Babic right away, the appellant, whether he has any issues he wishes to raise regarding his health. THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. As far as my health is concerned, my health is under control. I have treatment for my chronic illnesses. As for my other issues, I would like to address you in private session regarding that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That is about health. Any other matters regarding your status in detention, the facilities or any other matters you wish to raise? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. But could we please turn into private session for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel for the Defence, is that in agreement with your instructions that we go into private session since this is a public hearing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUELLER
utterances.text: I know. I was about to stand up and to ask you for a favour to give me the floor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Babic can sit down as counsel is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUELLER
utterances.text: Mr. Babic is probably making some comments on his, let's say, psychological situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUELLER
utterances.text: In particular, he's going to address the situation of his family.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUELLER
utterances.text: He kindly asked me to ask you for closed session. As you know, there is a particular problem perhaps if we do all this in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I see. All right. I would like to ask the Prosecution counsel whether there are any objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCKEON
utterances.text: No, there's no objection, Your Honour. I think it would be appropriate to have this portion of the hearing in a private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. May I ask the Registrar, please, to ask the relevant office for private session.
